input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG DEFIS - DEFENCE INDUSTRY AND SPACE. Summary: Fused Pnt Analyses Based on European Infrastructure. Description: The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT. This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: • To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) • To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences; • To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; • To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment • To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment. <br> Doc Title: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Research into the Perception of Young People at Music Events Regarding Safety, with a Specific Focus on Girls and Lgbti+ Young People. Description: This assignment concerns a current and in-depth analysis of the contemporary (music) event culture for young people in Flanders, with a special focus on the barriers to organizing events by young people themselves and on the other hand. safety perception of girls, young women and people from the LGBTQI+ community. The remarkable decline in visitor numbers and the increase in barriers to organizing something yourself make clear the need for research into underlying causes. This qualitative research will question young people themselves, as well as local authorities, youth work and other youth associations. In addition, recommendations for policy and local actors are made. This research is an update and deepening of the Party research 2002 and 2013. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Research into the Underlying Mechanisms of Lgbti+ Phobia and Gender Stereotyping Among Young People in Flanders. Description: This assignment fits within the Flemish equal opportunities policy plan 2026-2029, and more specifically within main objective 6: 'We increase the well-being and acceptance of LGBTI+ people.' Despite Flanders' relatively high score in terms of legal protection and social acceptance, LGBTI+ people continue to face exclusion, discrimination and violence in various areas of life. In addition, the prevention of gender-based violence remains a point of attention. There has been the last few years a noticeable increase in homophobia and a more rigid perception of gender roles among young people. This phenomenon appears to be related to a broader societal increase in anti-GBTI+ rhetoric and the rise of the manosphere and the femosphere. The JOP monitor1 and the research 'Enoeg - enough - assez' 2 map a disturbing evolution: • 18.3% of young people find aggression against LGBTI+ people acceptable (compared to 7.4% in 2018). • 92.6% of LGBTI+ young people surveyed reported at least one form of verbal or psychological violence. • 67.4% have experienced at least one form of sexual violence. • Boys show an increasing tendency to subscribe to strict gender roles, and the influence of online communities such as the manosphere contributes to reinforce stereotypical and discriminatory ideas. This evolution has consequences for the well-being of LGBTI+ young people and girls, such as more reports of physical and psychological violence and.... Published Date: 2025-10-25. Closing Date: 2025-11-26. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: Self Financed

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG ENER - ENERGY. Summary: Database, Monitoring and Research on Renewable Energy Auctions. Description: In the current context, auctions and tenders for public support to renewable energies are evolving rapidly. At EU level, changes in legislation have been agreed (Electricity Market regulation) and the Commission has issued recommendations and guidance on auction design to Member States. In addition, the Net Zero Industry Act has introduced provisions regarding the use of non-price criteria in such auctions. In the current practice, zero support auctions have become more common, non-price criteria are being increasingly used and technology-specific and hybrid auctions have become part of the toolbox, while the emergence of PPA markets also provides an alternative or complementary route to the financing of renewable energy deployment. In this changing landscape, decision makers in the EU and in the Member States need a clear reference point to source and exchange up-to date knowledge about the evolution of renewable energy auctions. The overall objective is to improve the effectiveness and cost-efficiency of these tendering procedures, taking into account the EU-s decarbonisation objectives. The project will: - Collect, organise, continuously update and make publicly available relevant data on renewable energy auctions in the form of a comprehensive free online auction database; - Provide empirical and theoretical analysis and concrete recommendations regarding the key aspects of the evolution of practice in renewable energy auctions, in particular all specific design features .... Tender Value: 1600000. Currency: EUR. Published Date: 2025-08-29. Closing Date: 2025-10-10. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

Summary: Longitudinal Support Contract on Specific Risks and Harms that Minors Face in the Eu Digital Environment over Time. Description: Amidst the upcoming adoption of Commission-s Guidelines on article 28(1) of the DSA as well as other measures on the protection of minors in Q3 2025, there is a need to increase our understanding of how the risks, harms and benefits that children experience on online platforms evolve (also in light of a potential review of the Guidelines in 2027). In addition, it is important to supplement currently fragmented understanding about children-s perceptions of their online experiences, or knowledge about what children would want from tech companies to improve their safety, security and well-being online. Complementing the EU-wide inquiry into the impact of social media on well-being, this support contract would help monitoring children-s perspective on how EU rules are improving the digital environment over time. The support contract aims at providing comprehensive and representative data on children-s online experiences in the EU over time, which would be accompanied by a monitoring measurement framework. Description: The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT. This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: • To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) • To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences; • To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; • To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment • To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment. <br> Doc Title: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG MOVE - MOBILITY AND TRANSPORT. Summary: Study on Seafarer-S Fatigue and its Relationship with Working Rosters on Ferries. Description: The objective of this comprehensive study is to methodically examine the issue of fatigue among seafarers working in various functions and capacities on ferries operating between ports of an EU Member State, between EU Member States and ports between EU and non-EU countries. Recognizing the central role of maritime safety, this research will examine how fatigue, influenced by different working rosters, impacts the well-being, performance, and safety of seafarers. Fatigue among seafarers not only poses a significant threat to their health and safety but also expose the safe operation of ferries, possibly leading to maritime accidents. This study should adopt a holistic approach, considering all elements that contribute to seafarers' fatigue, such as long working hours, insufficient rest periods, irregular shift patterns, and the demanding nature of work onboard on the ship. The primary focus, however, will be on the impact of working rosters on the fatigue levels of seafarers. By analyzing different roster schedules, including those with varying lengths and frequencies of shifts, the study should aim at to identifying patterns and correlations between specific roster configurations and the incidence of fatigue-related symptoms among crew members. The study should integrate biomedical measurements tools to assess the fatigue if possible. Description: Decarbonisation of international shipping is high on the agenda of the European Commission, with the Smart and Sustainable Mobility Strategy calling on the IMO to strive for high standards in the field of climate change. IMO adopted a number of measures to reduce GHG emissions from international shipping : the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII), the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) the Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP), the Data Collection System (DCS), the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI). A GHG Fuel Standard and an economical measure (so called Mid-term measures) must be adopted in 2025 for international shipping to reach the goals set in the revised IMO GHG Strategy (2023). A revision of the CII framework must be further considered at IMO after MEPC 83 and potentially of the EEXI and EEDI frameworks as well. Guidelines will need to be developed to implement the mid-term measures, as well as the SEEMP and the DCS. Additionally, the IMO has adopted and advanced guidelines on the life cycle GHG intensity of marine fuels (LCA Guidelines). Efforts are ongoing to refine and finalize these guidelines, including certification frameworks and addressing technical and sustainability aspects. The LCA framework will support the implementation of Mid Term Measures and need to be further developed to effectively inform and support the regulatory framework. Description: A growing number of Carbon Capture Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) projects are on track to become operational before 2030. This procurement is expected to establish and operate an open collaboration and knowledge sharing platform, providing data and up-to-date information about the entire CCUS sector, based on the collection of primary data from current and future large-scale demonstration projects. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG MOVE - MOBILITY AND TRANSPORT. Summary: Study on Seafarer-S Fatigue and its Relationship with Working Rosters on Ferries. Description: The objective of this comprehensive study is to methodically examine the issue of fatigue among seafarers working in various functions and capacities on ferries operating between ports of an EU Member State, between EU Member States and ports between EU and non-EU countries. Recognizing the central role of maritime safety, this research will examine how fatigue, influenced by different working rosters, impacts the well-being, performance, and safety of seafarers. Fatigue among seafarers not only poses a significant threat to their health and safety but also expose the safe operation of ferries, possibly leading to maritime accidents. This study should adopt a holistic approach, considering all elements that contribute to seafarers' fatigue, such as long working hours, insufficient rest periods, irregular shift patterns, and the demanding nature of work onboard on the ship. The primary focus, however, will be on the impact of working rosters on the fatigue levels of seafarers. By analyzing different roster schedules, including those with varying lengths and frequencies of shifts, the study should aim at to identifying patterns and correlations between specific roster configurations and the incidence of fatigue-related symptoms among crew members. The study should integrate biomedical measurements tools to assess the fatigue if possible. The goal of this study is to provide evidence-based insights that can feed policy initiatives, promoting enhanced seafarer well-being and ensu.... Tender Value: 200000. Currency: EUR. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG FISMA - FINANCIAL STABILITY, FINANCIAL SERVICES AND CAPITAL MARKETS UNION. Summary: Comparative Study on Best Practices for a Stronger Eu Sanction Enforcement. Description: Restrictive measures (sanctions) are an essential tool for the promotion of the objectives of the Common Foreign and Security Policy. Their objectives include safeguarding the Union-s values, maintaining international peace and security, consolidating and supporting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. The sanctions remain the main instrument in the Union-s toolbox to deter, prevent and condemn aggressive and illiberal behaviour of the third countries. Considering that the lack of sanction implementation, as well as inconsistencies across different jurisdictions of the Union, also represent a risk to Union financial interests and to the national financial systems, it is important to make sure that the Union sanctions are implemented equally across the Union. This is particularly relevant for the implementation of the Union sanctions against Russia, which have been subsequently adopted starting from 2014. In order to curb circumvention of Union sanctions and assist the Member States in their sanction implementation tasks, this pilot project concerns a study on the best practices and synergies that would benefit the Union-s sanction policy, taking stock of the examples of the United States- Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and the United Kingdom sanctions enforcement authority (OFSI). Summary: Comparative Study on Best Practices for a Stronger Eu Sanction Enforcement. Description: Restrictive measures (sanctions) are an essential tool for the promotion of the objectives of the Common Foreign and Security Policy. Their objectives include safeguarding the Union-s values, maintaining international peace and security, consolidating and supporting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. The sanctions remain the main instrument in the Union-s toolbox to deter, prevent and condemn aggressive and illiberal behaviour of the third countries. Considering that the lack of sanction implementation, as well as inconsistencies across different jurisdictions of the Union, also represent a risk to Union financial interests and to the national financial systems, it is important to make sure that the Union sanctions are implemented equally across the Union. This is particularly relevant for the implementation of the Union sanctions against Russia, which have been subsequently adopted starting from 2014. In order to curb circumvention of Union sanctions and assist the Member States in their sanction implementation tasks, this pilot project concerns a study on the best practices and synergies that would benefit the Union-s sanction policy, taking stock of the examples of the United States- Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and the United Kingdom sanctions enforcement authority (OFSI). input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: PARTNERSHIPS WITH BOARDS AND SOCIETY. Summary: Substantive Expansion Assessment Framework for Biodiversity in Construction Projects. Description: This assignment concerns the substantive expansion of the prototype of the assessment framework for biodiversity in construction projects. This prototype has been worked out by Embuild Flanders, and forms an objective framework for assessing the promotion of biodiversity in construction projects. This first version is only applicable for projects in urban context, and does not yet take into account the landscape integration into a wider environment, bodema speeches and the impact of measures taken for compensation off site. In order to achieve a supported result, it is requested to also test the calculation tool during the development process on 5 concrete pilot projects. The end result of this assignment consists of a user-friendly Excel calculation tool, with a clear manual and explanation for the formulas used. The intention is that these results will be integrated into one or more already existing online calculation tools in a subsequent phase. Description: The present document, including the annexes, constitutes the selection guide for the services of an advisor in the context of innovative construction for infrastructure projects. Specifically, the assignment primarily addresses the question of whether and how geopolymer concrete can be an alternative to conventional concrete, particularly in the design of a (bicycle) bridge and, secondly, parking lanes. The entire lifecycle of the chosen concrete type must always be considered (including sustainability and circularity aspects). Here, the term "geopolymer concrete" is understood to mean an alkali-activated binder without (or with a very small amount of) cement and with a low CO2 impact, generated by the reaction of calcium and aluminosilicate powders with an alkaline activator. This alkali-activated binder replaces Portland cement-based materials in conventional concrete. The use of mixtures with both high and low calcium content is permitted. Traditional cement types (CEM I to CEM V) are not included in this definition. The assignment will consist of, among others, the following tasks: (i) Advising on the application of geopolymer concrete; (ii) Assistance in the preparation of the testing program (indicative list see Annex 6 below); (iii) Conducting, monitoring, and analyzing a testing program with reporting; (iv) Checking whether and to what extent the calculation models of Eurocode 2 and the standards related to concrete (EN 206 + NBN15-001) are applicable or need to be ad.... To date, numerous stakeholders have called upon the Commission to advance and strengthen the EU-s just transition framework. In this context, this upcoming call for tenders seeks proposals for the establishment of an European Fair Transition Observatory in 2024. The Observatory is expected to facilitate the monitoring and implementation of fair transition policies across the EU, at all levels and involving key stakeholders, in different domains beyond coal intensive regions and sectors. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG EMPL - EMPLOYMENT, SOCIAL AFFAIRS AND INCLUSION. Summary: European Fair Transition Observatory (Efto). Description: The Council Recommendation on ensuring a fair transition towards climate neutrality was adopted by the Member States in June 2022, as integral part of the ‘Fit for 55- package. The Council Recommendation provides policy guidance to Member States on how to address the employment and social aspects of the transition and also outlines the commitment of the Commission to strengthen the knowledge base for policymaking and public debate related to fair transition. To date, numerous stakeholders have called upon the Commission to advance and strengthen the EU-s just transition framework. In this context, this upcoming call for tenders seeks proposals for the establishment of an European Fair Transition Observatory in 2024. The Observatory is expected to facilitate the monitoring and implementation of fair transition policies across the EU, at all levels and involving key stakeholders, in different domains beyond coal intensive regions and sectors. It will provide up-to-date information on fair transition policies, showcase best practice examples promoting fair transitions and strengthen the evidence base on fairness aspects of the transition through the collection and provision of relevant data and analytical work. <br> Doc Title: European Fair Transition Observatory (EFTO) <br> Contract Type: services. Summary: Single Framework Contract for the Provision of Technical Assistance and Financial/Economic Expertise in Support to the European Energy Efficiency Financing Coalition. Description: The European Energy Efficiency Financing Coalition (‘Coalition-) was announced in the EU ‘Save Energy- Communication, as a follow-up activity to the European Energy Efficiency Financing Group (EEFIG), which ceased activities in 2023. The Coalition has the objective of facilitating the mobilisation of private financing for energy efficiency in support of the 2030 and 2050 EU energy and climate objectives. This is in line with the ambition to step up investments in energy efficiency, expressed both in the European Council conclusions of 20-21 October 2022, and 15 December 2022, and the COP28-s pledge to double the global average annual rate of energy efficiency improvements from around 2% to over 4% every year until 2030. The legal basis of this initiative is Article 30(7) of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency (EED Recast). The aim of the Coalition is to establish a framework for dialogue and action between the European Commission, Member States, and Financial Institutions. The Coalition intends to adopt a market-oriented dynamic towards energy efficiency financing, with the ability to support the development of concrete projects at the national level. The Coalition was launched on the 22 April 2024. This framework contract intends to provide the Commission with support in the management and coordination of the upcoming Coalition activities. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DIEST. Summary: Community Management ' We Deliver 2.0 '. Description: We.Leveren.be is an existing local digital distribution platform for sending packages that are ordered at local web shops. It has been in use since 2022, with currently 100 local traders from Leuven and 6 neighboring municipalities ASL users. Shipments sent via this platform to local customers, do not travel unnecessarily to a large distribution center, but are processed and delivered locally. In addition, the packages are collected from local traders or in mail machines with an emission drivers and in a bundled collection round, in order to avoid maximum emissions. Packs with a destination outside the region will follow the normal flow. Once an order is completed with a trader, a shipping order can be created in Wij.Leveren. This is currently manually, via a .csv or via an API coupling (currently for Shopify, WooCommerce, Tilroy and Lightspeed C-Series). The platform automatically sends the data to the chosen courier service afterwards. Today they are bpost and a local bicycle courier, as part of this project it is still added. <br> Type: Services <br> Design and Execution of Research and Developme .... Published Date: 2024-07-18. Summary: Study on National Legal Framework and Obstacles for Asset Tokenisation in Member States. Description: The Digital Finance Strategy sets out the objective to ensure a technology neutral and innovation friendly regulatory framework. The Study would contribute to the specific objective set out in the FISMA management plan to ensure that opportunities from digital technology are widely employed to implement a safe, competitive and inclusive digitalisation of financial services. While there is considerable uncertainty around the future of crypto asset markets, a significant number of financial institutions see considerable potential in the tokenisation of traditional assets, both financial and other assets. The next Commission might therefore need to put a focus and possibly develop an asset tokenisation for the EU, which could possibly also be a project for cooperation with other services in the Commission. While with the DLT pilot the EU financial services regulation would not seem to be an obstacle, we understand from interactions with market participants and national authorities that there are a number of issues when it comes to national legislation in areas of private law and other aspects which may be standing in the way of asset tokenisation which the study should explore. This could then allow the Commission to follow up as part of possible future work on asset tokenisation. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG ENER - ENERGY. Summary: Study on Pass-Through Rate: Main Drivers, Country Differences and Policy Implications. Description: The European gas market changed markedly when the global economy recovered from the Covid-19 pandemic and due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. European gas prices increased to historically high levels after remaining broadly stable for more than a decade. As natural gas is widely used in energy production, energy became much more expensive also on the retail level for firms and households. Due to these events, the relationship between energy prices, inflation and the real economy stepped into spotlight. How do wholesale price shocks feed through to retail prices? The crisis of recent years has shown how understanding the pass-through rates and anticipating the retail sector-s reaction to wholesale shocks is fundamental to design efficient and effective markets and policies. Moreover, even when the crisis is over, the progressive phase-out of fossil fuels and deployment of variable renewable energy sources is expected to generate more volatility in wholesale markets. In this context, it is important to anticipate how this volatility may be transferred to retail prices and how this may affect consumer behaviour. Against this background, there is a limited understanding of how the pass-through rates work in practice, what are their main drivers and how they interact. The economic literature on the topic is relatively limited. Summary: Single Framework Contract for the Provision of Technical Assistance and Financial/Economic Expertise in Support to the European Energy Efficiency Financing Coalition. Description: The European Energy Efficiency Financing Coalition (‘Coalition-) was announced in the EU ‘Save Energy- Communication, as a follow-up activity to the European Energy Efficiency Financing Group (EEFIG), which ceased activities in 2023. The Coalition has the objective of facilitating the mobilisation of private financing for energy efficiency in support of the 2030 and 2050 EU energy and climate objectives. This is in line with the ambition to step up investments in energy efficiency, expressed both in the European Council conclusions of 20-21 October 2022, and 15 December 2022, and the COP28-s pledge to double the global average annual rate of energy efficiency improvements from around 2% to over 4% every year until 2030. The legal basis of this initiative is Article 30(7) of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency (EED Recast). The aim of the Coalition is to establish a framework for dialogue and action between the European Commission, Member States, and Financial Institutions. The Coalition intends to adopt a market-oriented dynamic towards energy efficiency financing, with the ability to support the development of concrete projects at the national level. The Coalition was launched on the 22 April 2024. This framework contract intends to provide the Commission with support in the management and coordination of the upcoming Coalition activities. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG ENER - ENERGY. Summary: Study on Pass-Through Rate: Main Drivers, Country Differences and Policy Implications. Description: The European gas market changed markedly when the global economy recovered from the Covid-19 pandemic and due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. European gas prices increased to historically high levels after remaining broadly stable for more than a decade. As natural gas is widely used in energy production, energy became much more expensive also on the retail level for firms and households. Due to these events, the relationship between energy prices, inflation and the real economy stepped into spotlight. How do wholesale price shocks feed through to retail prices? The crisis of recent years has shown how understanding the pass-through rates and anticipating the retail sector-s reaction to wholesale shocks is fundamental to design efficient and effective markets and policies. Moreover, even when the crisis is over, the progressive phase-out of fossil fuels and deployment of variable renewable energy sources is expected to generate more volatility in wholesale markets. In this context, it is important to anticipate how this volatility may be transferred to retail prices and how this may affect consumer behaviour. Against this background, there is a limited understanding of how the pass-through rates work in practice, what are their main drivers and how they interact. The economic literature on the topic is relatively limited. Summary: Study of Barriers to the Consolidation of and Reduced Fragmentation in Trading and Post-Trading Infrastructure. Description: The purpose of this lot is to explore barriers to consolidation of trading and post-trading infrastructure and potential ways to address those barriers identified. The assessment of the barriers should take into account vertical, horizontal and other types of consolidation among trading and post-trading infrastructure as well as explore the role that technology could play in removing those barriers. The assessment should also identify and characterise the synergies and operational cost reductions resulting from past consolidation. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DIRECTORATE-GENERAL FOR DEFENCE INDUSTRY AND SPACE (DEFIS), DEFIS.C.2 - SATELLITE NAVIGATION. Summary: Contribution to Radio-Navigation Accuracy and Resilience. Description: The main purpose of this project is to develop and optimize a fully functional ACAS (Assisted Commercial Authentication Service) pre-operational receiver and prototype server, with state-of-the-art technology and performance, and its demonstration in an operational environment including real GNSS authentication signals and with a dedicated testing platform. Such a platform has never been developed before and is considered as highly beneficial for ensuring ACAS correct implementation. It includes analysing critical aspects as hardware synchronization, form factor optimization, real-time signal authentication algorithms able to discern, to the extent possible, between natural impairments (e.g., multipath) and targeted interference, or client-server real-time connectivity. These developments contribute not only to adding resilience to satellite navigation but also to increase the accuracy of authenticated positioning. Summary: Development, Construction and Installation of a Vertical Demonstration Hydro Installation for Optimal Use of Space in Greenhouses. Description: The object of the contract is the development, construction and commissioning of a vertical demonstration multi-layer cultivation installation, including a warranty period. <br> Vertical cultivation installations are already being used in so-called plant factories, which are highly conditioned environments withoutglow. Today, with the exception of a few experiments, use in greenhouses is virtually non-existent and places new requirements on these systems in terms of climate conditioning (temperature, light, humidity), irrigation, inspection and control of planting material and ease of use (planting, harvesting, cleaning). The economic yield, on the other hand, is strongly related to the cost price of these vertical systems. There is also a need for innovation in this area to make these systems common in the market.<br> The intended demonstration cultivation installation comprises a self-supporting structure with several cultivation layers, adequate nutrition and watering, possibly moving parts, and control. The installation complies with all applicable norms and standards and is delivered including the necessary inspections. The safety tests are submitted to the client for evaluation. The contractor also providesa warranty period that at least meets the applicable legal requirements.<br> The research into the state of the art resulted in various available type architectures, each with advantages and disadvantages. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: INAGRO, EXTERNAL INDEPENDENT AGENCY OF THE PROVINCE OF WEST FLANDERS. Summary: Development, Construction and Installation of a Vertical Demonstration Hydro Installation for Optimal Use of Space in Greenhouses. Description: The object of the contract is the development, construction and commissioning of a vertical demonstration multi-layer cultivation installation, including a warranty period. <br> Vertical cultivation installations are already being used in so-called plant factories, which are highly conditioned environments withoutglow. Today, with the exception of a few experiments, use in greenhouses is virtually non-existent and places new requirements on these systems in terms of climate conditioning (temperature, light, humidity), irrigation, inspection and control of planting material and ease of use (planting, harvesting, cleaning). The economic yield, on the other hand, is strongly related to the cost price of these vertical systems. There is also a need for innovation in this area to make these systems common in the market.<br> The intended demonstration cultivation installation comprises a self-supporting structure with several cultivation layers, adequate nutrition and watering, possibly moving parts, and control. The installation complies with all applicable norms and standards and is delivered including the necessary inspections. The safety tests are submitted to the client for evaluation. The contractor also providesa warranty period that at least meets the applicable legal requirements.<br> The research into the state of the art resulted in various available type architectures, each with advantages and disadvantages. Summary: Survey on Antisemitic Attitudes in the European Union. Description: On 5 October 2021, the Commission presented its first-ever EU strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life that sets out a series of measures articulated around three pillars. The strategy indicates that the Commission will contract an EU-wide online survey on antisemitic prejudices. This contract aims to implement this action, by carrying out a representative survey, based on a state of the art questionnaire, that measures antisemitic attitudes among the general population, including key-subgroups such as based on educational level, migration background, gender, age, political preference (including the far left and far right), religion and belief. The survey should be sensitive to possible overlaps between these groups and provide insights in intersectional attributes to prevalent antisemitic prejudices among the general public. Summary: Counter-Uas Living Lab. Description: The application of drone (unmanned aircraft systems UASs) is becoming very popular in many areas with the implementation of the new drone regulations. However, there is potential for misuse of drones: they can be used to breach privacy, for espionage by using cameras or other sensors, to hijack telecommunication signals and in combination with biological or chemicals agents, explosives or other weapons they could harm persons, disrupt services and damage infrastructure. The JRC DRONE project is doing research on how to counter UAS around critical infrastructure. As part of this project JRC will setup a living lab for Critical Infrastructure stakeholders. It will demonstrate policy impact to identify needed policies around c-UAS, for research on c-UAS solutions, to develop processes, procedures and to link it to solutions. Description: The Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between the EU and six countries of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) has been applied since October 2016. output.Description: The application of drone (Unmanned Aircraft Systems UASs) is becoming very popular in many areas with the implementation of the new drone regulations. The JRC Drone project is doing research on how to counter UAS around critical infrastructure. As part of this project JRC will setup a living lab for Critical Infrastructure stakeholders. It will demonstrate policy impact to identify needed policies around c-UAS, for research on c-UAS solutions, to develop processes, procedures and to link it to solutions.
